subject: [Handoff] SDK Starter Kit + Integration checkpoints for Integrify
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@integrify.com>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@integrify.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Handoff: Integrify SDK starter kit + next steps

Hi Sofia / Monica —

Per the sync with Integrify this morning, quick handoff notes so CSM/Implementation can pick up the integration:

Summary:
- Integrify is aiming to replace their current on-prem LLM gateway with our Dedicated offering for lower token costs and a migration to Redwood SDK for client-side requests.
- Primary contacts: Sam Lee (Product Lead) and Alex Kim (integration engineer).
- Expected go-live target: November 3rd (tentative).

Attachments I dropped below: SDK starter kit (zip), integration checklist (pdf), and a small CSV showing their expected request/second patterns.

Key asks for CSM/Impl:
1) Provide an SDK quickstart (node + python) with sample code for endpoint migration + KV cache warmup guidance.
2) Outline a retry/timeouts strategy for their bursty webhooks — they peak at ~120 RPS but median is 6 RPS.
3) Confirm rate-limit posture and an agreed throttling policy to avoid 429 storms during cutover.

Immediate next step: Sofia, can you own the Implementation Plan & schedule a discovery with Alex this week? I added the Drive folder link and HubSpot deal in the metadata.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@integrify.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@integrify.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Integrify SDK starter kit + next steps

Hi Alex / Sam —

Nice to meet you virtually. Thanks Vivek for the summary. I’ll lead the implementation plan and run the discovery with Alex. Agenda proposals for our call:
- Quick architecture review (how Integrify currently calls the LLM gateway)
- SDK quickstart walk-through (Node + Python snippets)
- Migration cutover plan: blue/green vs. phased prefix traffic shift
- Retry, timeouts, and rate-limit enforcement pattern (and how Redwood Analyze will surface regressions)
- Required artifacts for Security/Procurement: SOC2 summary + network diagram (we’ll pull those into the Drive)

I attached a lightweight integration checklist and the SDK starter kit to this thread. Please download and confirm you can run the sample in your staging environment.

Pre-call asks (if you can send before our discovery):
- A small sample of request headers/body for your current gateway (sanitized)
- Typical payload size (median and 95th percentile token counts)
- Any hard SLAs for latency (P99 targets) or max retry budgets

Proposed slots: 2026-09-14 10:00am PT or 2026-09-14 3:00pm PT. Which works best?

Regards,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@integrify.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@integrify.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Integrify SDK starter kit + next steps

Sofia — thanks, I pulled the starter kit and ran the Node example. Quick notes / questions before the call:

What worked:
- The sample auth flow (API key env var) bootstrapped quickly.
- Streaming example matched our expectations for chat glue code.

Questions / Requests:
1) Retry semantics: The example uses exponential backoff with jitter, but we need a recommended policy for idempotent vs non-idempotent calls. Our webhook consumers will re-post on 5xx; we want to avoid duplicate ordering.
2) Timeouts: what should we set for connect vs read timeouts in high-latency regions? Our current gateway uses connect=1s/read=5s; we expect P95 latency of ~200ms after migration.
3) Rate limit headers: does Redwood return granular headers (x-rw-rlimit-remaining, x-rw-rlimit-reset) we can wire into our client?
4) Endpoint migration: can we get a short example to dynamically fall back to a secondary model variant if the primary is returning 503?

I’ll schedule the 3:00pm PT slot on 2026-09-14 and invite the team.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Kim
Senior Integration Engineer, Integrify
alex.kim@integrify.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@integrify.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@integrify.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: SDK Starter Kit + Integration checkpoints for Integrify

Sofia / Team —

Thanks for taking point, Sofia. A few items I want on the Implementation Plan checklist (high priority):

1) SDK examples: provide both optimistic and conservative templates.
   - Optimistic (low-latency, minimal retry): connect=1s, read=3s, retry=3 with exponential backoff (500ms * 2^n + jitter), mark non-idempotent calls to not retry.
   - Conservative (safety-first for webhooks): connect=2s, read=8s, retry=5 with capped backoff, de-dupe at consumer level using idempotency keys.

2) Endpoint migration pattern:
   - Phase 0: sandbox smoke tests (canary 1% traffic) with KV cache warmup for top 20 prefixes.
   - Phase 1: 10% traffic with adaptive batching off for first 1 hour, monitor P95 and 429s.
   - Phase 2: 50% traffic with batching enabled and warmed caches.
   - Rollback: immediate revert window with DNS TTL <60s or traffic split fallback.

3) Rate limit handling: ensure Integrify honors token-lever headers. We provide x-rw-remaining, x-rw-reset-seconds and a 429 body with a suggested retry-after window. Implement client-side leaky-bucket with a short-term burst allowance to absorb spikes.

4) Security/Procurement: I’ll attach SOC2 artifact to Drive and confirm the network diagram by EOD.

Sofia — after the discovery call, please produce a one-page Implementation Plan and a runbook for cutover with explicit owner assignments. Tag me if any SLA exceptions are requested; I’ll review credits/discount asks.

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Head of CSM Operations, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
